title: India-Russia Ties: Strategic Partnership and Changing Realities

scenes.text: Can an old friendship survive when both partners start finding new friends?
scenes.narration: Imagine your oldest school friend suddenly starts hanging out with your biggest rival. For decades, India and Russia called each other all-weather friends, but global geopolitics is now testing that special bond.

scenes.text: Childhood best friends sharing lunchboxes who now build separate social circles in college.
scenes.narration: Think of this as an everyday analogy: imagine two childhood best friends who shared everything in school. When they grow up and join different college groups, they still care for each other, but life gets much more complicated.

scenes.heading: Milestones of Indo-Russian Cooperation

events.what: Soviet aid for Indian basic industries
Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed
Yeltsin renegotiates friendship treaty without security clause
Partnership elevated to special privileged status

scenes.narration: Here is the historical journey: Moscow backed Indian industrial growth after 1953 and signed a historic friendship treaty in 1971. Even after the Soviet Union collapsed, both sides rebuilt ties into a special strategic partnership.

scenes.heading: Strategic Pillars Versus New Friction

columns.title: Traditional Pillars
items: Joint production of BrahMos supersonic missiles

columns.title: Growing Friction
items: Bilateral trade stuck around eleven billion dollars
Weapon sales of Sukhoi thirty-five to China

scenes.narration: On one hand, defense co-production like BrahMos missiles and nuclear plants at Kudankulam remain rock solid. But on the other hand, bilateral trade stays low at eleven billion dollars while Moscow conducts military drills with Pakistan.

scenes.name: Kanwal Sibal
scenes.idea: Complacency grew because both nations faced no serious problems.
scenes.narration: Former ambassador Kanwal Sibal explains a clever paradox: because India and Russia never had open disputes, both became complacent. Meanwhile, other powers quietly shifted the balance around them.

scenes.heading: Weighing Strategic Partnership
scenes.narration: Here's the trick to understanding foreign policy: India must balance its trusted historical friendship against Russia's growing pivot toward China and Pakistan. Prime Minister Modi reminds us that one old friend is better than two new ones.

items: Strategic partnership built on defense and nuclear energy
Bilateral trade and geography remain key structural challenges
Pragmatic balancing needed as Russia engages China and Pakistan
scenes.narration: To recap: first, defense and nuclear energy anchor this partnership. Second, weak trade and poor connectivity need urgent work. And third, smart diplomacy must safeguard India's security as regional dynamics shift.
